speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the characteristics of your neck swelling: is it hard or soft, painful or painless, and does it move when you swallow? Also, how long has it been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of colon cancer and this painless, progressive neck mass, are you experiencing any difficulty swallowing, breathing, or have you noticed any new lumps in your neck or under your arms?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Ultrasound, Neck_FNA_Cytology, Serum_TSH, T3, T4.
REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given your history of colon cancer; a normal ultrasound suggests the mass may not be thyroid-related or could be deep-seated. Has the swelling changed in size over the last week, and do you have any night sweats or unexplained weight loss? REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_With_Contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is unexpected; a normal CT scan effectively rules out a deep-seated metastatic mass or a large abscess in the neck. Given your history of colon cancer and the persistent swelling, could you describe the specific location of the lump relative to your cervical spine and sternocleidomastoid muscle? Are you experiencing any changes in bowel habits, such as constipation or a change in stool caliber, which might suggest a recurrence of your primary cancer elsewhere?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA, Abdomen_PET_Scan.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer with Unusual Presentation
